newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Oct 16.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Oct 16:

SAN DIEGO - Republican Bob Dole unleashed his most stinging attack of the presidential campaign, accusing President Clinton of diminishing the presidency through a pattern of evasion, half truths and "endless violations of public trust".

WASHINGTON - The Supreme Court accepted what promises to be a momentous case on religious freedom involving the constitutionality of a 1993 federal law that makes it far more difficult for government to infringe on religious practices.

DECATUR, Ga. - The anxiety ripping across the American electorate this year about education is widespread on the campus of DeKalb college where struggling to keep up with tuition costs has become a constant.
WASHINGTON - CSX and Conrail said they have agreed to merge in an $8.4 billion deal that would have a major impact on the Washington region and the East.

WASHINGTON - An assistant chief, a police chaplain and 16 other civilian employees and officers were suspended by the D.C. police department in connection with a federal investigation into an alleged fencing operation.
TOKYO - Japanese women aim for political equality as more vie in Sunday's election than at any time since 1945.
